title: Base change of a curve

proof.text: Curve over $k'$, first half. The structure morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated and of finite type [def-sc-curves]; its base change along $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the second projection $C_{k'}\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-base-change], which is therefore separated and of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] (Stacks Tags 01KU, 01T4).

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: 'Separation, ... finite type ... are all stable under base change'

proof.text: An affine open cover of $C_{k'}$. As $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type, $C$ is covered by affine opens $U_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ ($i\in I$) with each $A_i$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] (the definition, applied to the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}k$ of the target). Let $p:C_{k'}\to C$ be the first projection. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (with $S=U=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $V=U_i$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}k'$), $p^{-1}(U_i)$ is an open subscheme of $C_{k'}$ identified with $U_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$, which is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_kk')$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Since the $U_i$ cover $C$, the $p^{-1}(U_i)$ cover $C_{k'}$.

source.place: ## Proof, second paragraph: 'for an affine open piece $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $C$'

proof.text: Nonemptiness. If $C=\emptyset$ then $C_{k'}=\emptyset$, since $p$ maps it into $C$; then $\dim C_{k'}=\dim C=-\infty$ and clause 3 is void. If $C\neq\emptyset$: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is one point and $\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is nonempty, so $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and its base change $p:C_{k'}\to C$ along $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] (Stacks Tag 01S1); hence $C_{k'}\neq\emptyset$.

source.place: ## Proof, second paragraph (the dimension comparison needs both schemes nonempty)

proof.text: Dimension. Let $C\ne\emptyset$ (the empty case is step 3). By [lem-pc-dimension-affine-open-cover] applied to the cover $(U_i)$ of $C$ and to the cover $(p^{-1}(U_i))$ of the nonempty scheme $C_{k'}$ (step 2), $\dim C=\sup_i\dim A_i$ and $\dim C_{k'}=\sup_i\dim(A_i\otimes_kk')$. Each $A_i$ is a finite type $k$-algebra, so $\dim(A_i\otimes_kk')=\dim A_i$ by [lem-pc-dim-base-change] (Stacks Tag 00P3, whose proof is the blueprint's Noether normalization (00OY) and going-up (00GU) argument). Hence $\dim C_{k'}=\dim C$. These are the dimensions of [def-pc-dimension] (supremum of the dimensions of the local rings), which equal the Krull dimensions of the underlying spaces by [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings]; so $\dim C_{k'}=\dim C\le1$ in the sense of [def-sc-curves]. With step 1 and $k'$ algebraically closed, $C_{k'}$ is a curve over $k'$: clause 1.

source.place: ## Proof, second paragraph: 'by Noether normalization (Tag 00OY) ... finite morphisms preserve dimension (Tag 00GU) ... hence $\dim C_{k'}=\dim C$'

proof.text: Smoothness. If $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth, its base change $C_{k'}\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is smooth by clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change] (Stacks Tag 01VB).

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: 'smoothness ... stable under base change'

proof.text: Properness. If $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper, its base change $C_{k'}\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] (Stacks Tag 01W4).

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: 'properness ... stable under base change'

proof.text: Affineness. If $C$ is affine, $C\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a $k$-algebra $A$; since a fibre product is unique up to unique isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product], $C_{k'}\cong\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kk')$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], an affine scheme. With steps 5 and 6 this is clause 2.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: 'for an affine curve $C=\operatorname{Spec}A$ one has $C_{k'}=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kk')$'

proof.text: Connectedness. Let $C$ be a connected curve: nonempty, connected and of dimension one. Then $C_{k'}$ is nonempty (step 3) and of dimension $\dim C=1$ (step 4). The algebraically closed field $k$ is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed] (every nonconstant polynomial, separable or not, has a root in $k$). So the connected $k$-scheme $C$ is geometrically connected over $k$ by [lem-weil-separably-closed-geometrically-connected] (Stacks Tag 0363), and by the definition of geometric connectedness [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], applied to the extension $k'/k$, the base change $C_{k'}=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is connected. Hence $C_{k'}$ is a connected curve over $k'$: clause 3.

statement_change.old_statement:
Let $k\subseteq k'$ be algebraically closed and let $C$ be a
curve over $k$. Then $C_{k'}$ is a
smooth separated curve over $k'$ of the same dimension, and
$C_{k'}$ is proper (resp. affine) if $C$ is proper (resp. affine).
